#### Private Defined types

* `portage::atomfile`: Private: one file of atoms in a managed /etc/portage/<kind>/ directory.
* `portage::makeconf`: Private: renders a target's make.conf from a single hash.
* `portage::managed_dir`: Private: a directory under /etc/portage whose unmanaged content is purged by default.

### Data types

* [`Portage::Atom`](#Portage--Atom): A Portage package atom, e.g. `>=sys-apps/sed-4.8:0::gentoo`.
* [`Portage::Cronschedule`](#Portage--Cronschedule): A cron schedule for the cron type: minute and hour are required; the other fields default to `*` and `root`.
* [`Portage::Feature`](#Portage--Feature): A FEATURES token, optionally disabled with a leading `-` (see make.conf(5)).
* [`Portage::Keyword`](#Portage--Keyword): An ebuild keyword such as `amd64`, `~amd64`, `-amd64`, `*`, `~*` or `**`.
* [`Portage::Licensetoken`](#Portage--Licensetoken): A license name, `@GROUP`, or `*` wildcard, optionally negated with `-`.
* [`Portage::Makeconfig`](#Portage--Makeconfig): The make.conf variables documented in make.conf(5), with the type each accepts.
* [`Portage::Patchdir`](#Portage--Patchdir): A /etc/portage/patches/<category>/<dir> name: `cat/pn`, `cat/pn-ver` or `cat/pn-ver-rN`, each with an optional `:slot`.
* [`Portage::Resources`](#Portage--Resources): Resource name mapped to the parameters of that resource, minus `root`.
* [`Portage::Targetroot`](#Portage--Targetroot): A Portage config root: the host (`/`) or a chroot target.
* [`Portage::Token`](#Portage--Token): A single whitespace-free item of a space-delimited make.conf list.
* [`Portage::Uri`](#Portage--Uri): A fetch URI (`http`, `https`, `ftp`, `rsync`, `sftp`, `ssh`) or an absolute mirror path.
* [`Portage::Useflag`](#Portage--Useflag): A USE flag, optionally disabled with a leading `-`.

## Classes

### <a name="portage"></a>`portage`

Every parameter except `root` is passed to portage::target; see it for the
details of each. Hash parameters deep-merge across Hiera layers, and an
entry can be removed in a higher layer by prefixing its key with `--`.

Managed directories purge unmanaged files by default, so run
`puppet agent --test --noop` before the first apply on an existing node.

#### Examples

##### Hiera data

```puppet
portage::make_conf:
  MAKEOPTS: ['-j8']
portage::repositories:
  gentoo:
    sync_type: rsync
    sync_uri: rsync://buildhost.example.org/gentoo
portage::profile:
  path: default/linux/amd64/23.0/systemd
```

### <a name="portage--buildhost"></a>`portage::buildhost`

Each key of `targets` is a chroot under /var/lib/portage-targets; bootstrapping
its stage3 is out of scope. A target's hash takes the portage::target
parameters except `root`. Every target defaults to
`FEATURES="getbinpkg buildpkg binpkg-signing"` and an `upstream` binrepo with
signature verification; a target's own `make_conf` keys and `binrepos` entries
override those defaults (set FEATURES in a target to replace it entirely).

#### Examples

##### Hiera data

```puppet
portage::buildhost::targets:
  desktop:
    profile:
      path: default/linux/amd64/23.0/desktop/systemd
    make_conf:
      MAKEOPTS: ['-j8']
```

### <a name="portage--buildhost--mirror"></a>`portage::buildhost::mirror`

rsyncd.conf gets one read-only module per published repository, each rooted
at `${mirror_dir}/<repo>` (the snapshot portage-publish writes). The live
repositories under `repos_dir` are never exposed: `mirror_dir` may not
overlap them, and module paths can only point below `mirror_dir`.
Consumers sync with `sync-uri = rsync://<buildhost>/<repo>`.

### <a name="portage--buildhost--publish"></a>`portage::buildhost::publish`

Puppet only installs; it never runs a build. `portage-publish` syncs the
host's repositories, builds @world in every target one after the other, and
only when all builds succeeded copies the repositories to
`${mirror_dir}/<repo>` and each target's binary packages to
`${binhost_dir}/<target>`, then regenerates the binhost indexes. Repository
metadata is never regenerated, so the published tree stays byte-identical to
what the signed MetaManifest covers.

### <a name="portage--buildhost--signing"></a>`portage::buildhost::signing`

Each root gets a private GnuPG home at /etc/portage/binpkg-signing holding
the signing key, imported once with `gpg --import`. Portage signs with it
when the target's make.conf carries `$make_conf` (see below). The private
key is a Sensitive value and is redacted from catalogs, reports and logs.

`$make_conf` and `$public_key` are exposed for portage::buildhost, which
merges `$make_conf` into every target's make.conf, and for distribution to
consumers.

The private key is never purged: the GnuPG home lives beside, not inside,
any directory this module purges, and /etc/portage/gnupg (the getuto
keyring used for verification) is untouched.

#### Examples

##### Hiera data

```puppet
portage::buildhost::signing::roots:
  - /var/lib/portage-targets/stage3
portage::buildhost::signing::key_id: '0x40DCF18E97150795'
portage::buildhost::signing::public_key: |
  -----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----
  ...
portage::buildhost::signing::private_key: ENC[PKCS7,...]
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `portage::buildhost::signing` class:

* [`private_key`](#-portage--buildhost--signing--private_key)
* [`public_key`](#-portage--buildhost--signing--public_key)
* [`key_id`](#-portage--buildhost--signing--key_id)
* [`roots`](#-portage--buildhost--signing--roots)

##### <a name="-portage--buildhost--signing--private_key"></a>`private_key`

Data type: `Sensitive[Pattern[/\A-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----[\s\S]+-----END PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----\s*\z/]]`

ASCII-armored private signing key, supplied through eyaml.

##### <a name="-portage--buildhost--signing--public_key"></a>`public_key`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----[\s\S]+-----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----\s*\z/]`

ASCII-armored public key matching `private_key`.

##### <a name="-portage--buildhost--signing--key_id"></a>`key_id`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A(0x)?[0-9A-Fa-f]{16,40}!?\z/]`

Key ID or fingerprint Portage signs with (BINPKG_GPG_SIGNING_KEY); the
key must be usable without a passphrase.

##### <a name="-portage--buildhost--signing--roots"></a>`roots`

Data type: `Array[Portage::Targetroot, 1]`

Config roots to install the key into.

Data type: `Boolean`

Remove unmanaged files from the directory.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-portage--accept_keywords--purge_ignore"></a>`purge_ignore`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

File name patterns exempt from purging.

Default value: `[]`

### <a name="portage--binhost_key"></a>`portage::binhost_key`

The keyring is /etc/portage/gnupg in the target's root. It is never managed
as a file resource, so it is never purged: getuto initialises it once (only
getuto may create it, or it skips adding the Gentoo release keys and its
local trust key), then the key is imported and locally signed with getuto's
trust key so Portage accepts packages signed by it. getuto's refresh only
re-imports the Gentoo keys and refreshes existing ones from keyservers; it
never removes other keys.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `portage::binhost_key` defined type:

* [`root`](#-portage--binhost_key--root)
* [`public_key`](#-portage--binhost_key--public_key)
* [`fingerprint`](#-portage--binhost_key--fingerprint)
* [`filename`](#-portage--binhost_key--filename)
* [`purge`](#-portage--binhost_key--purge)
* [`purge_ignore`](#-portage--binhost_key--purge_ignore)

##### <a name="-portage--binhost_key--root"></a>`root`

Data type: `Portage::Targetroot`

Config root of the owning target.

##### <a name="-portage--binhost_key--public_key"></a>`public_key`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----[\s\S]+-----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----\s*\z/]`

ASCII-armored public key, e.g. `$portage::buildhost::signing::public_key`
from the build host.

##### <a name="-portage--binhost_key--fingerprint"></a>`fingerprint`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A(0x)?[0-9A-Fa-f]{40}\z/]`

Full fingerprint of the key (40 hex digits).

##### <a name="-portage--binhost_key--filename"></a>`filename`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*\z/]]`

Name of the stored key in binhost-keys/; defaults to the title minus its
`<target>/` prefix.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-portage--binhost_key--purge"></a>`purge`

Data type: `Boolean`

Remove unmanaged files from binhost-keys/.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-portage--binhost_key--purge_ignore"></a>`purge_ignore`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

File name patterns exempt from purging.

Default value: `[]`

### <a name="portage--set"></a>`portage::set`

Manages one package set file in /etc/portage/sets/ of a target.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `portage::set` defined type:

* [`root`](#-portage--set--root)
* [`atoms`](#-portage--set--atoms)
* [`world`](#-portage--set--world)
* [`filename`](#-portage--set--filename)
* [`purge`](#-portage--set--purge)
* [`purge_ignore`](#-portage--set--purge_ignore)

##### <a name="-portage--set--root"></a>`root`

Data type: `Portage::Targetroot`

Config root of the owning target.

##### <a name="-portage--set--atoms"></a>`atoms`

Data type: `Array[Variant[Portage::Atom, Pattern[/\A@[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*\z/]]]`

Package atoms and nested sets (`@name`) in the set.

##### <a name="-portage--set--world"></a>`world`

Data type: `Boolean`

Also list the set (`@name`) in /var/lib/portage/world_sets so that
`@world` includes it.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-portage--set--filename"></a>`filename`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*\z/]]`

Set name; defaults to the title minus its `<target>/` prefix.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-portage--set--purge"></a>`purge`

Data type: `Boolean`

Remove unmanaged files from the sets directory.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-portage--set--purge_ignore"></a>`purge_ignore`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

File name patterns exempt from purging.

Default value: `[]`

### <a name="portage--target"></a>`portage::target`

Inner resources are titled `<target>/<key>`, so targets never collide. Each
hash maps a key to the parameters of the matching defined type, minus `root`.
The directories those types manage purge unmanaged files by default;
/etc/portage itself is never purged, so /etc/portage/gnupg (the getuto
keyring) survives in every root.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `portage::target` defined type:

* [`root`](#-portage--target--root)
* [`make_conf`](#-portage--target--make_conf)
* [`repos_default`](#-portage--target--repos_default)
* [`repositories`](#-portage--target--repositories)
* [`profile`](#-portage--target--profile)
* [`binrepos_default`](#-portage--target--binrepos_default)
* [`binrepos`](#-portage--target--binrepos)
* [`binhost_keys`](#-portage--target--binhost_keys)
* [`package_use`](#-portage--target--package_use)
* [`accept_keywords`](#-portage--target--accept_keywords)
* [`licenses`](#-portage--target--licenses)
* [`masks`](#-portage--target--masks)
* [`unmasks`](#-portage--target--unmasks)
* [`package_envs`](#-portage--target--package_envs)
* [`envs`](#-portage--target--envs)
* [`sets`](#-portage--target--sets)
* [`patches`](#-portage--target--patches)
* [`postsync`](#-portage--target--postsync)
* [`purge`](#-portage--target--purge)
* [`purge_ignore`](#-portage--target--purge_ignore)

## Data types

### <a name="Portage--Atom"></a>`Portage::Atom`

Accepts an optional blocker (`!`, `!!`), a version operator (`<`, `<=`, `=`,
`>=`, `>`, `~`) with a version, a trailing `*` on `=` atoms, a slot with
an optional subslot and `=`/`*` slot operator (or a bare `:=`/`:*`), and a
`::repo` constraint.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A!{0,2}[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+.-]*\/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*(:[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+.-]*(\/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+.-]*)?[=*]?|:[=*])?(::[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)?\z/, /\A!{0,2}(<=|>=|<|>|=|~)?[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+.-]*\/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*-[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*[a-z]?(_(alpha|beta|pre|rc|p)[0-9]*)*(-r[0-9]*)?\*?(:[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+.-]*(\/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+.-]*)?[=*]?|:[=*])?(::[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)?\z/]`

### <a name="Portage--Cronschedule"></a>`Portage::Cronschedule`

A cron schedule for the cron type: minute and hour are required; the other fields default to `*` and `root`.

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  'minute'             => Pattern[/\A[0-9*,\/-]+\z/],
  'hour'               => Pattern[/\A[0-9*,\/-]+\z/],
  Optional['monthday'] => Pattern[/\A[0-9*,\/-]+\z/],
  Optional['month']    => Pattern[/\A[0-9A-Za-z*,\/-]+\z/],
  Optional['weekday']  => Pattern[/\A[0-9A-Za-z*,\/-]+\z/],
  Optional['user']     => Pattern[/\A[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*\z/],
}]
```

### <a name="Portage--Feature"></a>`Portage::Feature`

A FEATURES token, optionally disabled with a leading `-` (see make.conf(5)).

Alias of `Pattern[/\A-\*\z/, /\A-?(assume-digests|binpkg-docompress|binpkg-dostrip|binpkg-ignore-signature|binpkg-logs|binpkg-multi-instance|binpkg-request-signature|binpkg-signing|buildpkg|buildpkg-live|buildpkg-proactive|buildsyspkg|case-insensitive-fs|clean-logs|collision-protect|compress-build-logs|compress-index|compressdebug|config-protect-if-modified|dedupdebug|distlocks|downgrade-backup|ebuild-locks|fail-clean|fakeroot|fixlafiles|force-mirror|getbinpkg|gpg-keepalive|home-dir-template-copy|icecream|installsources|ipc-sandbox|jobserver-token|keeptemp|keepwork|lmirror|merge-sync|merge-wait|metadata-transfer|mount-sandbox|multilib-strict|network-sandbox|network-sandbox-proxy|noclean|nostrip|notitles|observability|packdebug|parallel-fetch|parallel-install|pid-sandbox|pkgdir-index-trusted|preserve-libs|protect-owned|python-trace|qa-unresolved-soname-deps|sandbox|selinux|sesandbox|sfperms|skiprocheck|split-elog|split-log|splitdebug|strict-keepdir|stricter|suidctl|test|test-fail-continue|unknown-features-filter|unknown-features-warn|unmerge-backup|unmerge-logs|unmerge-orphans|userfetch|userpriv|usersandbox|usersync|warn-on-large-env|webrsync-gpg|mirror|news|noauto|nodoc|noinfo|noman|strict|xattr|sign|digest|distcc|ccache|candy|cgroup)\z/]`

### <a name="Portage--Keyword"></a>`Portage::Keyword`

An ebuild keyword such as `amd64`, `~amd64`, `-amd64`, `*`, `~*` or `**`.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A(\*\*|[~-]?\*|[~-]?[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*)\z/]`

### <a name="Portage--Licensetoken"></a>`Portage::Licensetoken`

A license name, `@GROUP`, or `*` wildcard, optionally negated with `-`.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A(-?\*|-?@?[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9+_.-]*)\z/]`

### <a name="Portage--Makeconfig"></a>`Portage::Makeconfig`

Lists are arrays and are space-joined when rendered (`USE_ORDER` is
colon-joined). Deprecated variables (PORTDIR, PORTDIR_OVERLAY, SYNC,
PORT_LOGDIR, PORT_LOGDIR_CLEAN) are intentionally absent.

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional['ACCEPT_CHOSTS']                       => Array[Portage::Token],
  Optional['ACCEPT_KEYWORDS']                     => Array[Portage::Keyword],
  Optional['ACCEPT_LICENSE']                      => Array[Portage::Licensetoken],
```

### <a name="Portage--Patchdir"></a>`Portage::Patchdir`

A /etc/portage/patches/<category>/<dir> name: `cat/pn`, `cat/pn-ver` or `cat/pn-ver-rN`, each with an optional `:slot`.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+.-]*\/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*(-[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*[a-z]?(_(alpha|beta|pre|rc|p)[0-9]*)*(-r[0-9]+)?)?(:[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_+.-]*)?\z/]`

### <a name="Portage--Resources"></a>`Portage::Resources`

Resource name mapped to the parameters of that resource, minus `root`.

Alias of `Hash[String[1], Hash[String[1], Any]]`

### <a name="Portage--Targetroot"></a>`Portage::Targetroot`

A Portage config root: the host (`/`) or a chroot target.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A\/\z/, /\A\/var\/lib\/portage-targets\/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\z/]`

### <a name="Portage--Token"></a>`Portage::Token`

A single whitespace-free item of a space-delimited make.conf list.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[^\s"]+\z/]`

### <a name="Portage--Uri"></a>`Portage::Uri`

A fetch URI (`http`, `https`, `ftp`, `rsync`, `sftp`, `ssh`) or an absolute mirror path.

Alias of `Variant[Stdlib::HTTPUrl, Stdlib::Unixpath, Pattern[/\A(ftp|rsync|sftp|ssh):\/\/[^\s"]+\z/]]`

### <a name="Portage--Useflag"></a>`Portage::Useflag`

A USE flag, optionally disabled with a leading `-`.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A-?[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9+_@-]*\z/]`
